[2023 summer phd probability — problem 2]

Part I, Exercise 2. Let $X$ be a discrete random variable valued in $\{1, 2, \dots, n\}$ with $P(X = j) > 0$ for all $j$.
For any integer $k \in \{1, \dots, n-1\}$ and events $E = \{X \ge k\}$, $F = \{X \ge k+1\}$, prove $\mathbb{E}[X \mid E] \le \mathbb{E}[X \mid F]$.

Let p_j=P(X=j), and B={X=k}. I want to express E as B ∪ F. If α=P(B|E) and β=P(F|E), then α + β = 1, where both α and β are greater than 0.

Using the conditional total expectation, I can develop E[X|E] accordingly. I'll justify the calculations to finalize everything neatly.
response.text:
Let \(p_j=\mathbb P(X=j)\), with \(p_j>0\) for all \(j=1,\dots,n\). Fix \(k\in\{1,\dots,n-1\}\), and define

\[
E=\{X\ge k\},\qquad F=\{X\ge k+1\}.
\]

Then \(F\subset E\), and inside \(E\) we have the disjoint decomposition

\[
E=\{X=k\}\sqcup F.
\]

Since \(p_j>0\) for every \(j\), both \(\mathbb P(E)>0\) and \(\mathbb P(F)>0\), so the conditional expectations are well-defined.

Using the law of total expectation over the partition \(\{X=k\}\) and \(F\) of \(E\),

\[
\mathbb E[X\mid E]
=
k\,\mathbb P(X=k\mid E)
+
\mathbb E[X\mid F]\,\mathbb P(F\mid E).
\]

Let

\[
\alpha=\mathbb P(X=k\mid E),\qquad 1-\alpha=\mathbb P(F\mid E).
\]

Then

\[
\mathbb E[X\mid E]
=
\alpha k+(1-\alpha)\mathbb E[X\mid F].
\]

Because \(F=\{X\ge k+1\}\), we have

\[
\mathbb E[X\mid F]\ge k+1>k.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\mathbb E[X\mid E]
=
\alpha k+(1-\alpha)\mathbb E[X\mid F]
\le
\alpha \mathbb E[X\mid F]+(1-\alpha)\mathbb E[X\mid F]
=
\mathbb E[X\mid F].
\]

Hence

\[
\boxed{\mathbb E[X\mid E]\le \mathbb E[X\mid F].}
\]

In fact, since \(p_k>0\), we have \(\alpha>0\), and since \(\mathbb E[X\mid F]>k\), the inequality is strict. Thus

\[
\mathbb E[X\mid E]<\mathbb E[X\mid F].
\]
